country_overview: Nigeria operates a managed floating exchange rate regime administered by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN). The Naira is subject to significant exchange controls, particularly on capital account transactions and foreign currency access for residents.

summary.traveler: Travelers may bring in foreign currency without limit but must declare amounts of USD 10,000 or equivalent. Export of foreign currency is restricted and subject to CBN rules.
summary.business: Businesses must route all significant foreign exchange transactions through authorised dealer banks. Capital repatriation and certain payments require CBN approval or documentation.

rules.bring_foreign_currency_in: Foreign currency may be brought into Nigeria without limit. Amounts of USD 10,000 or equivalent must be declared to Nigerian Customs upon arrival.
rules.take_foreign_currency_out: Foreign currency may be taken out up to the amount declared on entry or supported by authorised dealer documentation. Residents are subject to strict CBN limits.
rules.cash_declaration_threshold: USD 10,000 or equivalent in foreign currency or negotiable instruments at entry and exit. Declaration to Nigerian Customs is mandatory.
rules.resident_holding_rules: Nigerian residents are subject to CBN limits and approval requirements when holding or using foreign currency accounts. General unrestricted access requires specific authorisation.
rules.non_resident_rules: Non-residents may open and operate foreign currency accounts and transfer funds more freely through authorised dealer banks.
rules.business_invoicing_settlement: Cross-border business transactions must be settled through authorised dealer banks in accordance with CBN foreign exchange regulations.
rules.exchange_controls: Nigeria maintains a managed exchange regime with significant controls on capital account transactions. Current account transactions are subject to documentation and reporting requirements.
rules.banking_conversion_practicality: Foreign exchange conversion is available only through authorised dealer banks. Access to foreign currency is tightly regulated and often subject to availability.
